newsitem.title: FRANCE: Valeo head says "no change in direction".
newsitem.headline: Valeo head says "no change in direction".

text.p: A change in the ownership of French car parts maker Valeo, announced earlier, will not mean a change in strategy, chairman Noel Goutard said on Tuesday.

"There is no change in direction," he told a news conference. The priority will be a "strong and healthy balance sheet", and the company will pay particular attention to pursuing "controlled and profitable growth", he said.
French holding company CGIP earlier said it is buying 20 percent of Valeo from investment group Cerus for 4.7 billion francs and wants a more active dividend and acquisition policy.
Goutard insisted that Valeo would not make compromises on the health of its balance sheet but would seek to balance the imperatives for growth and financial health.

He added that Valeo had acquired companies in the past but had relied on its own resources and had not been able to raise capital from the markets as Cerus did not want to see its 27.4 percent stake diluted.
But with the new ownership structure, Valeo would be free to tap the markets for funds when it saw acquisition opportunities, he said.

CGIP's purchase of the bulk of Cerus' stake meant "the identity and integrity" of Valeo was preserved, he said. The change in ownership had the support of Valeo's main European customers, particularly French firms, as well as its U.S. clients, he added.

The chairman of PSA Peugeot Citroen, Jacques Calvet, has fought a long battle to ensure the Valeo stake did not fall into the hands of U.S. companies which had shown interest in buying the Cerus holding.
Besides CGIP, French state-owned Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) is raising its Valeo stake to 5.4 percent from 1.9 and the JP Morgan GT Corp fund is taking 3.6 percent for up to five years.
